sam: heads-up: p95 on r-infer-06 spiked ~3x around 11:14 UTC. Top callers are long prompt requests with tool calls. Kernel fallback count jumped, kvcache miss rate doubled. Anyone on eng-runtime awake?

priya: seeing same on metrics. spikes coincide with a tenant that has lot of streaming tool calls (external API retriever). Pod CPU also higher. Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood/pg/xyz :eyes:

infra-bot: deploybot: rolled out runtime change rtm-1.13 to pool r-infer-06 at 10:58 UTC

jon: can we get a flamegraph? ran pprof on instance r-infer-06-03 for 60s:

```text
# top 10
30.2% kernel_selector()
22.1% continuous_batch_loop()
15.5% kv_cache::miss_handler()
8.7% tensor_copy_async()
5.0% cuda_kernel_generic()
```

priya: interesting — kernel_selector fell back to generic_cuda for long sequences due to incorrect seq_len bucket heuristics after the rollout.

maria: I see tool-calling loop in request logs: user keeps calling llm->tool->llm leading to chained long prefixes. That blows up KV cache effectiveness because prefixes not reused. Example log: [request_id: abc123] 'call_tool: web_retriever', 'resume: chat' x4

jon: repro: run loadgen with mix: 5% tool-loopers, 95% short chat. With current batching heuristic, batcher waits 50ms to fill expected batch but tool loop requests are single long sequences -> increases tail latency. Proposed: lower max wait for small batch sizes + detect tool loop via repeated tool header and force non-batching.

priya: quick mitigation: revert rtm-1.13 kernel selection change, and reduce batch_wait_ms from 50->20 for r-infer pools. Will open PR and deploy canary.

sre-oncall: making change, canary to r-infer-06-04 starting in 2m. If p95 drops back to baseline, we rollback globally.

maria: also adding K/V cache hit-rate alert and extra logging for request lineage to detect tool loops. Follow-up: perf postmortem and unit test for seq_len bucket.

sam: thanks. assigning action items: priya -> PR + rollback, jon -> batching heuristics patch, maria -> logging + alert, jon & priya -> perf regression test in CI. We'll sync in 30m if canary shows improvement. :thumbsup:
